cells.remarks: Issued from Pravarapura. Records the royal grant of the village Charmmāṅka situated on the bank of the river Hiranyā- madu-nadī in the Bhōjakata-rājya and which consisted of 8000 (nivartanas) of land by the royal name to thousand brāhmaṇas, of which only fortynine are mentioned by name. The grant was made at the request of Kōṇḍarāja, the son of Satyāgrahā, who was the senāpati. Published in ibid., pp. 22 ff., and Plate.

cells.remarks: Registers a grant of the village Muṇḍa-rājyagrāma in Kōriyalā-12, excluding the devadāya and brahmadāya land in to Mādhava- paṇḍita, son of Gōkarṇa-paṇḍita, hailing from Hastigrāma in Madhyadēśa and belonging to the Pārāśara gōtra and Vasiṣṭha-pravara-gōtra. It is stated that the lands granted were capable of yielding 300 drammas of income annually. The record was written on the orders of the king by Jōgapaiya, who was the son of the brother of Bhaḍḍē- gāre-mukhya-śrī Nāgāḷaiya. Mahāmātya Daddhapaiya and Śrī-Jōgala-mukhya-śrī-Sōḍhala are also mentioned. Published in Ep. Ind., Vol. XXXVII, pp. 247 ff.

cells.date: Nandivardhana Śaka 882 (current), Raudra (Northern cycle), Vaiśākha śu. di. 1, Āshāḍha śu. di. 3, Wednesday, Rōhiṇī, 959 A.D., April 18, f.d.t. 18.
cells.remarks: States that after conquering the South and uprooting the Chōlās (Chōda dynasty, the supreme power in peninsular victorious (vijaya-rājye) of Nelpāṭi in order to distribute among them, at Chōda, and Siblab, territories conquered by him, to accept tribute of the conquered, and to arrange for the construction of the Krishnēsvara and Gauja-mārttāṇḍa Āditya temples in the vicinity of Setu and the construction of Viśvakaśvaras and other temples in the Kuṇḍali maṇḍala in the village of Chintā maṇḍala in Rikkati, situated in Alaṭ go-700, a sub-division of Naṇḍerī vishaya, as brāhmaṇas, for his parents' and his own merit, to Guṇdabhata, son of Bhaṭṭi-deva-bhaṭṭu. The donee stated to have been a resident of Ghaṭapallikā, born of Karṇāṭa-viśaya and belonging to the Ātrēya-gōtra and Bāhvricha-śākhā. The writer of the charter was Yōddhyamma. Published in JBRAS (New Series), Vol. X, pp. 21 ff., and Plate.

cells.remarks: States that on the representation of the Vaḍḷakaramaḷu of Oṇṭimiṭṭa that they were prevented by the Balijas from mounting the car on the day of the car festival of god Tirumala, the chief of the place, while camping at Tirupati, having enquired about the matter and finding the truth in this regard at Tirupati, bestowed upon them (i.e. the Vaḍḷakaramaḷu community of Oṇṭimiṭṭa) the same rights as they had enjoyed from the days of Peda-Tirumala-rāyya. Cf. further Source of Vijayanagara History, Vol. II, p. 368.

cells.remarks: Records the creation of a settlement (palli) called Digva- Trupati situated to the west of the village Kōlakonda endowed for the angarapaṭi services of god Mallikārjuna and the grant of half the income from the village for the merit of the king by Vengalaraju of Chennakesvara of Kōlakonda for the merit of the king, by Basavaraju of dāṇāyaka of Haritasa-gōtra, Āsvalāyana-sūtra and [Rik]- sākhā. cells.place:
Vaḍakkappattu.—Temple of Agastīśvaram.
Northern wall of the first prākāra; central
shrine, west and south walls, second tier.
cells.remarks: Stones disarranged and portions lost. Commences with the king's praśasti, Tiruvaṇḍanatilakam...-viḷambaram etc. Records gift of land made and purchased from his seat Pāṇḍyarājan in the hall Alagiyapāṇḍyan-kūḍam of the palace in [Ti]ruppavāṇṇam, granting 107 mādai being half the income from Munnūruvamaṅgalam, a brahmadeyam in Nīlī-nāḍu, pākkuvatti from Jēvat[t]iruppu, and 5 kalams for the daily food offerings to god Mahādēva of Kumārit-Tiruvagattīśvaram in Purattaya-nāḍu. The order was issued at the instance of Kainbi-nāļvān representing Sattan Nārāyaṇan alias Tiru-vagattīśvarayogil, of the temple. Noticed in the Topo-graphical List of Travancore Inscriptions, No. 9, or Nos. 8 and 12 also.

cells.place: Rock in a field to the south of the temple of Agastīśvaram.

cells.remarks: The lines of the writing run from bottom upwards. Opens with an invocation to the Buddha and gives the mythical genealogy of Pallava, the founder of the Pallava dynasty. Verse 8 gives the popular etymology of the name Pallava. Then are given the names of seven Pallava kings: Mahēndravarman, his son Viṣṇugōpa, his son Siṁhavarman, his son Aṅkavarman, then Utrarvarman, then Siṁhavarman, son of Siṁhavishṇu and lastly Siṁhavarman. The incomplete prose passage at the end states that Siṁhavarman on his return from an expedition to the north, came to a place called Dhaṇyaghaṭaka, sacred to the Buddha. Further details are lost, the stone being broken here. In characters of about the 11th century. Published in Ep. Ind., Vol. X, pp. 43-44, and Plate and in SII, Vol. I, No. 32.

In characters of about 200 B.C. Lüders' List, Nos. 1329-31.

cells.place: Chakkara-ppalli, Chakravāhēśvara temple, central shrine, south wall and pīṭha.
cells.remarks: Records the sale of land made tax-free to god Sīrya-dēvar for whom a temple was built in Chakkara-ppalli by Adittan of Chakkara-ppalli, a resident of Vettakkudi, the kīlāvan of Poṉṉig-i-nūl-in, by the sabhaiyār Agaliyamangalam, a brāhmaṇadēyam in Kīlār-kūrram. The land endowed is stated to have been rendered fallow by the breaching of the banks of Kāvēri to the west of the temple. The land was sold for the benefit of the soul of king Rājakesari, who died in the golden palace (poṉmāligaittuñjina). In characters of the 10th century.

cells.place: Slab in the Kannada Research Institute Museum. Findspot: Bhalkal, Bhalkal Petha, North Kanara District.
cells.date: Śaka 1472 (nātra-m-hēra-vṛddhi-vidhu), Saumya, Vaiśākha ba. 8, Sunday = 1549 A.D., May 19, f.d.t. 11.
cells.remarks: Contains a detailed genealogical narrative of the Śāḷuva family of Hiḍuvali. Records the construction of a basadi, named after himself as Chēma-chaitya, at the instance of his wife, Vīrāji, the Śāḷuva queen, and the installation of the image of Vīra-Jina. The stanzas are stated to have been composed by Varddhamānaśakhi.

cells.location: Bammigasāhi
cells.place: Slab kept in the compound of the village Panchayat Office.
cells.remarks: Damaged. States that the king was ruling over Palas[ige]-1200 and Konkaṇa-900. Contains a eulogy of Mahāsāmanta Surgaṇipa (also mentioned as Sūryamayya), who is described as dharamaparāyaṇa and is administering Bharani-12, another 12 division (name lost) and Kampala and records that his minister Singa caused a Jina-bhavana to be constructed at Honnehalli and that he also made grants of land, housesites and probably a perpetual lamp. The grants were received by Ananta-vīryra Siddhānta-munīśvara of Yapanīya sangha and Kundūr gaṇa.

cells.location: Belvantara
cells.place: Slab kept in front of the Chalukya of Kalyāṇa Jagadēkamalla II temple of Kalmēśvara in the village.
cells.date: Śaka 1072, Śukla, Chaitra śu. 7, Monday, saṅkrā- maṇa. Irregular.
cells.remarks: Records a grant of land for offerings to god Hadavāḷēśvara after laying the foot of Vāsēvara-paṇḍita, the disciple of Vāmadēva-paṇḍita, known as Ēkōjīkarāvarati, the disciple of Vāmadēva-paṇḍita. Vāyamabhudēva of Muḷugunda and Hēgaḍē Kāvaṇa, dāṇḍanāyaka of Kōḍe, the administrator of Tammayūru-Pannir- Nāyakka and ruler of Noḷukunda situated in Māvaḷe-500 Kāvāṇa is stated to be the subordinate of Daṇḍanāyaka Māḍirājayya, the administrator of Tammayūru-Pannir- Pppali, Māvaḷi, Kōḍe, Kiruvatti, Kaggavige, Ammanagay pbhāvi and Nīlagunda, and also subordinate of Mahāmaṇḍalēśvara Ēśvara Vīra Permāḍi, the son of Kadamba II. Jayakēśi II and Maīaladēvī, and ruler of Komkana-900, Palasige-12,000 and Kavadidvīpa-savilakka. Also records the gift of a shop on the road by the merchants probably to the same deity. Mentions Vāmadēva-paṇḍita-dēva, the disciple Vīśvēśvara-paṇḍita and further records grant of land by the merchant, Mārōja.

cells.location: Malkankoppa
cells.place: Slab set up on the bank of the tank in the village.
cells.remarks: Registers grants of lands, gardens, houses, an oil-mill and a tolge of oil from the remaining oil-mills to the basadi constructed by him, by Bammisetti alias Bennemana of Puligere belonging to the Sāgainā family. Mentions Mādeyyanāyaka, the dandanāyaka of Vāṅgala, Mahāmaṇḍaleśvara Kārya-gāvuṇḍa, while Mahāmaṇḍaleśvara Cāguṇḍēva (Gūhalladeva) was administering the area. A jigaraige (jīgarije) i.e., a piece of cloth used by ascetics during their practice of penance, was also donated to the basadi by Ekkācāra-varigouda. Stipulates that the grants made were to be protected by the aruvattokkalu, the gauṇdas and the vasudhīvaras.

Mentions Mādeyyanāyaka, the dandanāyaka of Vāṅgala, Mahāmaṇḍaleśvara Kārya-gāvuṇḍa, while Mahāmaṇḍaleśvara Cāguṇḍēva (Gūhalladeva) was administering the area. A jigaraige (jīgarije) i.e., a piece of cloth used by ascetics during their practice of penance, was also donated to the basadi by Ekkācāra-varigouda. Stipulates that the grants made were to be protected by the aruvattokkalu, the gauṇdas and the vasudhīvaras.Read more (1 KB)

cells.place: Slab lying in the field of Parasappa Kallappa Hullakuļi.
cells.date: Chālukya-Vikrama, Viśvāvasu, Māgga-sira śu. 5, Thursday. Uttarāyana saṅkramaṇa=1126 December 20.
cells.remarks: States that Kadamba Jayakeśi was ruling over Konkaṇa-900, Pālasige-12,000 and Kavadadvīpa-savlākṣa and states that Mahāmaṇḍaleśvara Hākī-balla, the husband of Amaladevī, was ruling over Kēvula-12,000. Mentions Baim-chayya and his younger brother Rāchamalla-nāyaka, the two ministers of Hākīballa, Jayakeśi-chāmuṁpa, the ruler of Tammiyūru alias Tambrapūra, his younger brother Jayakeśi-danṇāyaka. Records that Baim-chayya and Rāchamalla-nāyaka caused to be con-structed a Jainā-basadi at Tammiyūru and also that he made a grant of land to the basadi after offering respects to Jayakeśi-dandanāyaka and mahārājādhirāja-māndēva of Mūla-saṅgha and Sūrastha-gaṇa. Also records 'gifts by the Nakharas, Teļigas and the paropājīvakas (i.e. botol-leaf traders) to the same basadi.

cells.remarks: Records a gift of land to the basadi constructed by Pērgade Bammachayya by the Yaḍḍa vyāpāri Bandhu varmayya of Pāṇungal after offering respects to Māḍiri- jayya-daṇḍanāyaka of Tammayūru and Narasiṅgadēva of Kōḍe. Mentions the gift of land to the basadi in No. 407 above. Also records a grant of tax income on certain specified commodities in the Māvaḷiya-thāṇe, to the same basadi by Sunkavērgade Nārāyaṇanayaka and Timm- ayyanna-gauṇḍa and others of the village (names lost) and Tīgēya (gardeners). States that Muḍḍa-Bammōjja and the grandson of Jātōja was the engraver and that Mādiyana was the writer.

cells.location: Siddhanabhāvi
cells.place: Slab set up in the field of the church belonging to the Basel Mission.
cells.remarks: Fragmentary. Registers a grant of land to god. Saṅgamēś- vara by Sīmōja Kaggā alias. Kaggava alias Hēggaḍē Kāvāṇa, son of Kēśava and Padumiyakka. Refers to a daṇḍanāyaka (name lost) and ruling from Panni- r-Nāyakka and Noḷukunda and also subordinate of Mahāmaṇḍalēśvara Ēśvara Vīra Permāḍi, the son of Kadamba II. Jayakēśi II and Maīaladēvī, and ruler of Komkana-900, Palasige-12,000 and Kavadidvīpa-savilakka. Also records the gift of a shop on the road by the merchants probably to the same deity. Mentions Vāmadēva-paṇḍita-dēva, the disciple Vīśvēśvara-paṇḍita, probably the priest of Saṅgamēśvara. In characters of about the 12th century.

cells.date: Chālukya Vikrama śu. 1, Sunday, Uttarāyaṇa saṅkrā- nti=1126 A.D., December 27. The saṅkrānti occurred on December 25.
cells.remarks: Refers to the emperor's son-in-law, Kadamba Jayakēśi, as ruling over Koṅkaṇa-900, Palasige-12,000 and Kavada- dvīpa-savilakka and states that Mahāmaṇḍalēśvara Hāki- balla, the husband of Kamalādēvī, by Muḍḍugunde and Hēḷḷa- gūḷuṇḍa of Huḷigūḍu, Muḍḍa-gauṇḍa is stated to be the son of Chāyigauṇḍa of Sīgalavanna and a subordinate of Mahāmaṇḍalēśvara Pormāḍidēva of Kaḍamba-vaṁśa. Nēma- gauṇḍa is mentioned as the son of Muḍḍagauṇḍa. Towards the end, a grant of one perpetual lamp is recorded.

cells.date: Śaka 1094, [Aśka] year 4, Dhanus ba. 4, Monday=1172 A.D., November 6.
cells.remarks: Fragmentary. Records the installation of a perpetual lamp for the god Kīrtivāsa i.e., Śiva by Bāḷi-Kāchchōṭika, described as lopādāna, Saivāchārya and Rājaguru, for the salvation of tapōdhana Sāṇḍhāripāda probably a priest of the god Uttārēśvara. cells.remarks: Commences with the king's praśasti. Tirumalaḍi-uḍaiyār-kōil etc. Records that having assembled in the temple of Tiru- vāyppāḍi-Āḷvār in their place on the day, the Perunguri- sabhaiyār of Kāyakkūḍi, a brahmādēya in Kurumbūr-nāḍu in Jayangoṇḍa-śōḷa-vaḷanāḍu, exempted from taxes the lands mentioned in favour of the deity Tribhuvanamudaiyār-dēva set up in the temple of Tirunalaḍi-uḍaiyār, by Dēvan Bhu- vanimāṇikkam, a servant of the royal household (Uḷagu- ḍaiyār-agapparivāral-peṇḍāṭṭi). It is said that the above sabhai received 50 kāśu for this purpose from the temple treasury.

cells.place: South wall, outside
cells.remarks: Commences with the king's praśasti Tiruvaiyāru etc. Records an undertaking by some Śivabrāhmaṇas of the temple of Tiruvaiyāru-uḍaiyār in Muḷaiyūr-nāḍu of the Uyyakkoṇḍār-vaḷanāḍu to provide for the food offerings during the early morning worship, out of 45 kalaṃ of paddy which is stated to be the annual interest on 45 aṇḍu-nāṛkāśu which they had received perhaps in some regnal year of Rājēndra I from Komman, a vēḷān of Veḷḷāḷan of Viliyūr in Muḷaiyūr-nāḍu in Uyyakkoṇḍār-vaḷanāḍu. The endowment made by Tidan Komman is also referred to while giving the details of this record.

cells.remarks: Records that a certain Vōhōrā Lakshmīnārāyaṇa, son of (name not clear), of the Vōhōrā-jāti, Kacchavāchha-gotra with three longings to Māṇḍalānī-śākhā (Māḍhānī-śākhā) of the Yuvarāja (Yajurveda) died fighting on the first date and was installed therein near the pond in the Yōga-ka hēḍa in the city of Pavattasar (Parbatsar), by Sutra (i.e., Sūtradhāra) Kēdāranātha, on the second date. cells.date: Vikrama 1989 (for 1869), Śaka 734, Subhakṛit, Dakshiṇāyana, Aṡvi- vūna śu. 5, Saturday =1812 A.D., Octo- ber 10.
cells.remarks: Records that at the instance of Chimanjī Raghunātha, younger brother (Bhaījī Rāo, Governor) of Madhavarāo (Mahādajī), the Sevak (Amaldār), (Anandīrām), (Gaokari), (the Seva) khāskhilā and Phaṭachinga Chāyrakavāla (Pakhārsingh Gāckwār), an official at Baroda (i.e. Baroda) assembled at Ahmadābād and heard a representation, made by the local people, including Sevak/Amaldār and others, to the effect that a certain property in question seems to relate to succession to property of a person, which was accepted by the assembly and an order proclaimed accordingly. Seems to mention an official of the Kupani (i.e., East India Company).

cells.remarks: Records the reconstruction of the dilapidated temple of the Sun by Malladēva, son of Rājasiṁha, daughter of Sōḍhalā and wife of Sōḍhalā and died fighting for Khān-i-A'zam when Jīnadgath was besieged by Pātasāhi Mahammadā (Muhammad Tughlak). Ibid., No. 731.

cells.place: Stone slab in the Archaeological Museum, from Gwalior, Mandsaur, Mandsaur Tahsil and District.
cells.remarks: Late. Records the construction of a śēpa, a well, a charitable water-stall (prapā), and a garden (ārāma) by Dattabhaṭa, who is described as the commander of the army of the ruler and the son of Vāyurakṣhita who in turn was the commander of the Gupta emperor Gōvindagupta, son of Chandragupta. The composer was Ravila. Published in Ep. Ind., Vol. XXVII, pp. 12-18, and Plate.

cells.location: Morena District Seopur Tahsil Dubkunda
cells.place: Stone slab lying in the ruins of a temple.
cells.date: Vikrama 1145, Bhādrapada śu. 2, Monday=1088 A.D., August 21.
cells.remarks: In two parts. The first part gives an account of the genealogy of the king, while the second records the foundation of a temple by the king and the grant of a village (grāma) and a garden with a well (i.e., a tax) on each śēpī (gunny bag of grain?) of the produce of a piece of land in the village of Mahāchakra capable of being sown with four śēpīs of wheat and a garden with a well to the temple of the king or for the purpose of the construction of the temple and for keeping it in good repair as well as for worship there. Also states that the king made provision of oil for lamps and for anointing the bodies of holy men. The name of the priest was Udayarāja and its engraver was Tilhaṇa. Published in Ep. Ind., Vol. II, pp. 232 ff.

cells.date: (1) Phālguna ba. 10, Thursday. (2) Vikrama 1886, Chaitra śu. 1.
cells.remarks: Records that Lāḍhūbhāī, wife of Ṭhākura Guṇasiṁhaji belonging to the Paṁvāra (Paramāra) [caste], who hailed from Mēvāḍa-pargaṇā and resided in Rāmagaḍha of śōpura (śivapurī) in memory of her first husband Ṭhākura Chaturbhuja was constructed in her memory and her other Ṭhākura śrī-Dēvīsiṁhaji of Pāvara on the second date. Mentions the names of officials like Bhāusāheba. The mason was Uvata śyōkisana (i.e., śivakṛiṣhṇa).

REWA DISTRICT
HUZZUR (REWA) TAHSIL
Rewā.—Stone slab. Firstspot: Kastura Tank in the same Tahsil.
cells.date: Kalachuri-Chēdi 944, Bhādrapada su. 1, Friday=1193 A.D., July 30.
cells.remarks: Records the excavation of a tank and its completion at the cost of 1500 pañchakas bearing the figure of Hanumān by Mahāsāmanta Dhīra, who had the superintendence of the works. Gives the genealogies of the king, the chief and the superintendent. The composer of the record was Purushōttama, son of Divākara and grandson of Rāma- chandra, to whom is referred theveras of the temple and an inhabitant of Klēsa. The reason was Ananta, son of Gāhaṇa. Mentions pratīhāra Dalha[m], son of Ra[l]ha. Published in CII, Vol. IV, pp. 346 ff., and Plate.

cells.location: Udaypur
cells.place: Qāḍī-ki-Masjid. North wall, outer face.
cells.language: Arabic prose and Persian verse and prose, Nasta‘līq.
cells.remarks: State that the mosque in the qasba of Udaypur situated in the Chandori province of Mālwa, on the border of Gondwāna, was commenced by Qāḍī Auliyā, son of Sayyid ‘Abdu-ṣ-Ṣamad, in the reign of Abū-l-Muẓaffar Nūru’d-Dīn Muḥammad Jahāngīr Bādshāh, but the mosque was not completed as Qāḍī Auliyā died before the mosque was finished, whereupon, after a year, Sayyid Ambiyā strove for its completion, but he also died in the meantime, and ultimately, Sayyid Ḥumām and Sayyid Dā’ūd, sons of Sayyid Auliyā, completed it in the first year of Shāh Jahān’s reign. The chronogram gives the date of the death of the Qāḍī and Makānī (sic), i.e. emperor Jahāngīr. Date that of writing (?). Cf. Ind. His. Quar., vol. III, No. 4 (1927), pp. 715-18, plate.

cells.place: Loose slab in the Tahsil office. Originally from a platform near the KotwālǮ.
cells.date: Regnal Year 23 (A. H. 1090), Ramaḏān 14=1679 A.D., October 3.
cells.remarks: Bilingual. Fragmentary. States that the maḥājans, traders and Brahmins of the gegāra (pargana) made a representation to the emperor that the levy on on landed property (ǫāgīr) was being recovered, a royal decree (faqīr decree) was issued under the orders of the emperor laying down that the levy was illegal and should not be taken. It also states that, in pursuance of that order, the faujdār Ībn-i-Raiṣān Khān (also designated as ‘āmgīrniṣīn) to stop levying those imposts, and as a result, (the amount of the levy) like ḿāṣā, baṣā', ḿātā, khonā', tolā, kotwalī, etc., half was remitted and the remaining half, being accepted by the concerned on their free-will, is to be well, while the taxes on butchers and wine-sellers were totally remitted, in accordance with a curse of 'Alīl and Rām for the Muslim or Hindu violators. For the Nāgarī portion, see No. 247 of Appendix B of A. R. Ep., 1966-67.
